item.title: South Korean schools embrace Great Books model against AI
item.description: In the South Korean city of Chuncheon, schools are experimenting with the 'Great Books' educational model from St. John's College in the US. Students read classic texts, such as Frankenstein, and debate them without the help of the internet or AI chatbots. Teachers do not lecture but only facilitate discussion. item.title: Grinch's heart grows three sizes in classic Christmas tale
item.description: In the classic story How the Grinch Stole Christmas, the Grinch begins with a heart that is „two sizes too small". Disguised as Santa Claus, he steals all the toys, food and decorations from the Whos and plans to throw everything off a mountain. item.title: Chef Goldberg cooks 100 meals every Tuesday at Toronto food bank
item.description: Since 2021, chef Maddy Goldberg has been cooking 100 hot meals every Tuesday for visitors to the Fort York Food Bank in Toronto. Goldberg initially studied social work before entering the hospitality industry, but missed the feeling of helping others. item.title: Ora-pro-nobis enriches the vegetable garden with protein-rich leaves
item.description: The Ora-pro-nobis, a thorny climbing plant, offers a fresh perspective on vegetable gardening thanks to its exceptional nutritional value. Brazilian laboratories analyzed the leaves and found approximately 22% protein on a dry matter basis, or roughly 2 grams of protein per 100 grams of fresh product — more than most traditional leafy vegetables. item.title: Algae diet makes wild fish unnecessary in fish farming
item.description: Researchers at the University of California Santa Cruz have developed a fully algae-based feed for farmed fish that could make wild fish redundant in fish feed. Farmed salmon and trout are currently often fed wild-caught sardines, herring, anchovies or mackerel, which contributes to overfishing. Globally, at least 20 million tonnes of wild fish are processed into fish feed annually. In...

item.title: Elk hunter saves wedding with dirt bike after highway closure
item.description: Erich Thalacker and Kyla Dickey rode into the Sawtooth Mountains in Idaho on their wedding day for a bridal photoshoot in dress and suit. item.title: Chef Maddy Goldberg cooks weekly for a hundred homeless people with food bank ingredients
item.description: Every Tuesday, chef Maddy Goldberg from Toronto prepares a meal for a hundred people in need, made from random ingredients she finds at the local food bank. In videos, she creates restaurant-quality dishes, such as lentil fritters with caramelized onion, cinnamon and curry powder. Goldberg initially studied social work, but discovered her love for cooking and ended up in fine...

item.title: Rhino dung becomes paper and protects the animals
item.description: In Assam, India, father and daughter Mahesh Chandra Bora and Nisha Bora founded Elrhino Stationery, a company that makes paper from the dung of rhinoceroses and elephants. The idea emerged after Mahesh read about similar paper production in Rajasthan. Local communities around nature parks such as Kaziranga and Pobitora collect the dung, which after washing and cooking is processed into...

item.title: Son tracks down writers of comfort letters to wounded Vietnam veteran
item.description: In 1967, 33 schoolchildren from Massachusetts wrote letters to Navy corpsman Russell Jacobson, who had suffered 12 gunshot wounds and shrapnel injuries in Vietnam. Severely wounded and unable to speak, he lay in Chelsea Naval Hospital, where he refused food and water. The letters, organized by a nun through St. Ann School in Gloucester, helped him recover. item.title: Hollow tree offers bats winter shelter
item.description: A hollow or rotting tree in the garden may look like dead wood, but it actually provides a valuable refuge for wildlife. In autumn, bats, which feed primarily on insects, actively search for food to build up fat reserves for hibernation. This period is also their mating season: after mating, the female stores the sperm until spring, when fertilization finally...

item.title: 86-year-old Carole Wade once sang backup for Elvis impersonators
item.description: Carole Wade (86) went viral last year when she sang Fleetwood Mac's „Landslide" during a karaoke afternoon at a senior center in Dallas, moving the audience. Less known is that Wade, who has been singing her entire life, once provided backup vocals for three different Elvis impersonators, including Steve West, with whom she worked for more than twenty years. item.title: Audrey Hepburn refused to have her wrinkles removed
item.description: Audrey Hepburn was known for her classic beauty and accepted aging with grace. She always rejected plastic surgery and was proud of her wrinkles. During her work as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador, photographer John Isaacs selected a photo showing her smile with wrinkles. item.title: Common garden birds recognize faces and sometimes bring gifts
item.description: Many people unknowingly have a small nature reserve in their backyard, with birds such as robins, house sparrows, cardinals, jays and tits. Although these birds are less famous than crows or ravens, they turn out to be surprisingly good at building bonds with humans. Some birds even perch on people as soon as they have gained trust, and can leave...

item.title: British shopkeeper Ada Le Poidevin's wartime resistance act on Guernsey revealed 40 years later
item.description: The courage of British shopkeeper Ada Le Poidevin, who hid three British soldiers on Nazi-occupied Guernsey during the Second World War, has come to light forty years after her death. Her 79-year-old niece Liz Walton uncovered the story thanks to photographs, diaries and data from Ancestry.com. In 1940, Le Poidevin and her husband Walter Bourgaize sheltered three stranded British servicemen...

item.title: CAR-T therapy helps patients with stiff person syndrome walk again
item.description: A cell therapy originally developed against cancer is proving helpful for stiff person syndrome, a rare autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the central nervous system. In an early study led by neurologists at Mayo Clinic, patients who previously needed assistance to walk and perform daily tasks regained enough function after a single CAR-T cell therapy treatment (mivocabtagene...

item.description: In Parc des Madelinots in the Verdun neighbourhood of Montreal, the soundscape is no longer dominated by traffic noise alone. item.title: Allison Raskin writes romcom with two protagonists living with OCD
item.description: Writer and comedian Allison Raskin is releasing her sixth book, 'Compulsively Yours', featuring two main characters — Libi Newman and Nate Keller — who both live with OCD. item.title: Young great horned owl survives 70 miles trapped in truck in Pennsylvania
item.description: A young great horned owl was struck by the truck of driver Ashley Moffitt while she was traveling 65 miles per hour in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. The bird became wedged in the truck's air deflector and remained there until Moffitt stopped 70 miles down the road. Employees at Old Dominion Freight Line in Carlisle freed the owl, which was unable...

item.title: Mother cat brings kittens to hospital in Izmir
item.description: A stray cat that had been fed by hospital staff in Izmir, Turkey for some time suddenly carried one of her kittens inside one morning. She walked fearlessly through the corridors, seeking help. Staff members examined the kitten and its siblings together with a veterinarian. The kittens were found to have an eye infection that prevented them from opening their...

item.title: Therapist's advice 'run the dishwasher twice' strikes a chord
item.description: A woman shared a story on Quora about her therapist that went viral after counselor Danielle Wunker posted it on Facebook. When she was going through a difficult period and couldn't even do the dishes, her therapist advised her to simply run the dishwasher two or three times instead of scrubbing the dishes first. item.title: Chester Zoo saves endangered Malaysian peacock pheasant chicks with foster mother and rubber glove
item.description: Chester Zoo was the only zoo in Europe this year to successfully hatch a Malaysian peacock pheasant. Only 15 of these endangered birds are being raised in captivity across European zoos. When a young mother abandoned her first egg, keepers placed it with a bronze-coloured peacock pheasant, who took on the role of foster mother. A second egg was hatched...

item.title: Florist in Cuincy places unsold flowers on forgotten graves
item.description: A flower shop in Cuincy doesn't throw away its unsold flowers from All Saints' Day. Instead, the owner takes them to the cemetery, where she places them on graves that appear to have been forgotten. The gesture of solidarity has moved many people online.

item.title: Aromatic herb border brightens vegetable garden without spending money
item.description: With three simple and free tricks, you can keep an aromatic herb border in your vegetable garden structurally sound, harmonious and highly productive. A quick check after rainfall or storms, manual weeding along the edges and regular compost application are sufficient to achieve results. This approach requires no extra investment yet ensures a well-organized and fertile vegetable garden.

item.title: November is the month to plant winter vegetables
item.description: Don't put away your garden tools just yet: November is a strategic month for the vegetable garden. It's the ideal time to sow and plant six extremely hardy vegetables. item.title: Eleven trees and shrubs should not be pruned this autumn
item.description: To get through the winter well, eleven common tree and shrub species are better left unpruned entirely in autumn. Cutting wood or branches during this period causes the plant to lose its flower buds directly or makes its overall structure more vulnerable. By refraining from pruning in the fall, these species remain stronger and better protected against the cold months...

item.title: Heat pump leasing saves French families €9,800
item.description: From November 17, 2026, lower-income French households can lease a heat pump with an average subsidy of €9,800, financed through the CEE scheme. The decree, published on November 10 in the Journal officiel, bundles installation, maintenance and electricity consumption into a single monthly payment, comparable to the old heating bill. After two to three years, the unit is paid off...

item.title: Solar parks in Gobi Desert reduce sandstorms
item.description: A new Chinese study shows that solar parks in the Gobi Desert slow down dust storms and improve air quality in cities downwind. The 42 solar parks, together covering more than 13,000 square kilometers, reduce monthly dust emissions by 352,400 tons. This is because the panels stabilize the soil, increase vegetation, and lower wind speed at ground level, acting as...

item.description: Synthetic fertilizer is produced in factories operating at 450°C and releases around 450 million tons of CO2 annually.
